summary: Multiprocess Python SDK seed reuse causes duplicate downstream tool side-effects on retry
description:
Issue summary:

Customer BrightCart reports repeated duplicate downstream side-effects (webhook triggers and order emulation calls) when using the Redwood Python SDK from a multiprocessing worker pool. Behavior is intermittent but reproducible under high throughput.

Impact:
- Duplicate downstream calls cause BrightCart to create duplicate order drafts in their fulfillment system (~0.3% of requests during load test).
- Affects production traffic for dedicated customer cluster in us-east.
- Business impact: manual reconciliation required; customer paused high-volume batch job.

Environment:
- Python 3.11 on Debian 12 (glibc), running in container with host-level fork semantics.
- SDK: redwood-python-sdk v1.10.2 (pypi).
- App uses multiprocessing.Pool with spawn/forkserver configuration; also observed with fork on older hosts.
- Model: redwood-instruct-large-v1 on dedicated pool.

Steps to reproduce (minimal):
1) Start a small Python worker script that forks 4 worker processes and uses the SDK to invoke a model with a function/tool call that triggers a webhook on completion.
2) Ensure workers send multiple rapid requests (1000 requests across workers).
3) Introduce transient network error on one request (simulate by dropping connection) to cause SDK retry logic to replay request from the client process.
4) Observe duplicate webhook deliveries downstream for some requests.

Expected behavior:
- SDK-generated idempotency keys or server-side dedupe should prevent duplicate external side-effects for retried function/tool calls.

Actual behavior:
- Duplicate executions observed when processes are forked: the SDK appears to generate identical idempotency tokens across different child processes (or reuse PRNG state), leading to replayed requests being accepted as new by downstream systems.

Attachments / logs:
- Customer provided request traces showing identical idempotency header values across processes (redacted).
- Container startup logs and a small repro script attached to the ticket (link provided by customer).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: Python PRNG state inheritance after fork is causing SDK idempotency token generator to produce duplicates. The SDK uses a seeded RNG (uuid4 based on random) in v1.10.2 and does not re-seed in child processes. In forked environments the RNG internal state is copied, so multiple processes can emit the same sequence of 'random' ids until reseed occurs.

Engineering repro: reproduced locally using a simplified harness that forks workers and triggers retries by blocking the response socket briefly. Observed identical idempotency tokens in ~0.2-0.5% of runs under heavy concurrency.

Immediate mitigation proposed: document and recommend customers either (a) pass application-managed idempotency keys per request, or (b) set environment variable REDWOOD_SDK_IDEMPOTENCY_RESOLVE=secrets to force use of os.urandom/secrets module. A patch is being prepared to change the token generator to use secrets.token_urlsafe() which is safe across forks.

Related PR: https://github.com/redwood/py-sdk/pull/987 (fix: use secrets/os.urandom for idempotency tokens + reseed on multiprocessing events).
comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10: Customer opened ticket after noticing duplicate order drafts during nightly batch. Collected traces and initial repro script. Marked as P1 because production impact and manual reconciliation overhead.
Eng (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Reproducing locally with containerized forked processes. Hypothesis: RNG state copied on fork. Will confirm ASAP and provide workaround.

Customer (BrightCart SRE - Anika Rao) 2026-03-11: Provided container image and small test harness. Confirmed that switching to a single-threaded client eliminated duplicates; multiprocessing pool triggers duplicates within minutes under load. Appreciate timely fix.

Eng (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-11: Patch created to replace random-based token generation with secrets.token_urlsafe() and explicit reseed on fork events. Running unit and load tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood/py-sdk/pull/987

Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12: Workaround sent to customer: 1) set environment variable REDWOOD_SDK_IDEMPOTENCY_RESOLVE=secrets OR 2) explicitly provide idempotency_key per request. Customer testing shows workaround removes duplicates in their staging environment.
Eng (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-12: Rolling patch to staging and scheduling hotfix release for py-sdk v1.10.3. Follow-up to add entry to SDK docs about multiprocessing and idempotency best practices.
resolution: Workaround provided (use secrets-based token or supply application-level idempotency key). Patch merged to py-sdk (PR #987) to use secrets.token_urlsafe and to reseed on fork. Hotfix scheduled for v1.10.3 release. Follow-up: add docs section and create an internal test harness for forked-process scenarios.
follow_up_actions: Release py-sdk v1.10.3 with RNG fix and reseed behavior
Add docs guidance: idempotency with multiprocessing and recommended patterns
Add CI job to run SDK idempotency tests under fork/worker pool conditions
Monitor BrightCart production for 72 hours and confirm no further duplicates
